properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-18: "should we consider approximations in reflow2 designs? In physics, approximations are not 'guesses' — they are mathematically precise tools used to simplify complex equations, isolate the core physics of a system, and make unsolvable real-world problems solvable. While mathematicians value exactness above all else, physicists value utility. … knowing how much precision you can safely sacrifice to make a calculation possible."
He named four kinds:
- neglecting minor effects (air resistance on a falling rock);
- Taylor expansion (small angle, sin θ ≈ θ, which makes a pendulum a harmonic oscillator);
- perturbation theory (Earth's orbit, then Jupiter's and Saturn's tugs);
- extreme limits (v ≪ c collapses relativity to Newton).
He added a plot showing sin x and x overlapping near 0 and diverging past about ±0.5 rad.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (found through the hub, 2026-10-18):
- flo2-calc dec:idea-an-approximation-is-chosen-and-justified (accepted 2026-10-04): whether an approximation holds is the agent's and the person's judgement. flo2-calc computes the validity metric and the error at a point.
- reflow2 req:assumptions-are-first-class (accepted): an assumption can stop being true, and what rests on it is computed.
- reflow2 dec:idea-can-a-design-hold-the-external-premise-it-rests-on (settled): outside premises dated and cited; the design never models the world.
- Since 0.86.0: assumed and discharged premises, `conditional` claims, and budgets with contributions and units (budget_report).

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) AN APPROXIMATION IS AN ASSUMPTION WITH A REGIME. Its validity condition is stated as a quantity (e.g. |θ| ≤ 0.3 rad). reflow2 compares it with the design's own operating range (a Constraint, a budget, a requirement's limit, units checked). When the design operates outside the regime, the approximation reads broken and everything resting on it reads unsupported. This catches the classic silent failure: the small-angle formula used at 40°.
(b) THE ERROR IS A BUDGET CONTRIBUTION. An approximation's error bound (e.g. |sin θ − θ| ≤ θ³/6 at the operating limit) is a contribution to the design's error or margin budget. budget_report then shows how much precision was spent on simplification, beside measurement uncertainty. This is "how much precision you can safely sacrifice", made a number.
(c) A NEGLECTED EFFECT IS A DECISION CONCLUDED BY ITS REASON. "Ignore air resistance" is a Decision whose chain rests on a computed magnitude ratio (drag/weight < 1% over the regime, a kept flo2-calc record). If the regime grows, the ratio's record no longer covers it and the decision loses support. This uses build phase 1/2 (a decision concluded by its chain).
(d) flo2-calc COMPUTES THE BOUND, not only the error at a point: e.g. the maximum of |sin θ − θ| over an interval, or a Taylor remainder bound, proven like calc's other rounded results. This is the calc design's side; its settled rule (judgement stays with the person) holds.
(e) MODELS RELATED BY LIMIT OR PERTURBATION. A relation between two models: "model A is model B in the limit v/c → 0", or "B = A + a perturbation of order ε", so a design can say which model it uses and when it must switch.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- THE AGENT / REFLOW2 LINE, and flo2-calc's settled decision: CHOOSING an approximation and judging it adequate is the person's or the agent's. What reflow2 and calc can own is the checkable part: the regime against the operating range, the error bound against the budget. Nothing here has reflow2 decide that an approximation is good.
- MOST OF IT IS ALREADY HERE. (a), (b) and (c) are assumptions, constraints, budgets and decisions-with-chains that exist or are being built (phases 1–2). A served recipe ("how to record an approximation") may be most of the value at almost no cost. FEWER THINGS (dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well).
- CHAOS IS DIFFERENT. The three-body problem is not tamed by a series: long-term behaviour needs numerical simulation whose error GROWS. That belongs to pairing a design with a domain simulator (dec:idea-an-mcp-around-xrt-so-a-beamline-design-is-ray-traced-not-asserted), not to this idea.
- "NOT A GUESS" IS TRUE ONLY INSIDE THE REGIME. An approximation used outside its regime IS a guess with a formula's authority. That is exactly why (a) checks the regime and does not just label the premise "approximate".

SIZE, as a finding:
- (c) small: a recipe plus phases 1–2;
- (b) small: budgets exist;
- (a) small to medium: comparing a stated regime with an operating range;
- (d) medium: a calc operator;
- (e) large: a new kind of relation between models.

A WORKED CASE to try on, beside his plot: a pendulum clock design whose period requirement rests on sin θ ≈ θ, with a maximum swing as a Constraint, the error θ³/6 from flo2-calc as a budget contribution, then "raise the swing" as the what-if.
